item.title: 2026 Research Analyst
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Fund seeks dynamic and highly motivated Research Analysts (RAs) with strong quantitative and analytical skills. The successful candidates should have the proven ability to work independently, as well as collaboratively in a team environment. The RAs will be responsible for a wide range of support including, but not limited to, data gathering, econometrics, analysis of economic or statistical data sets, and basic programming for high-quality analyses. This is a contractual appointment for one year, renewable for up to four years of cumulative contractual service, depending on the business need and performance of the incumbent. Research Analyst positions are filled with candidates physically residing in the local Metropolitan Washington, D.C. area. Job Summary Supports departmental objectives on economic analysis and managing information technology & systems. Analyzes and computes statistical and economic data in support of the department. Additionally, the RA will manage Fund database(s) and contribute to staff reports. This opportunity may meet PREDOC requirements for applications to subsequent academic study. Major Duties and Responsibilities Compiles statistical data, compares and evaluates alternative data sources, and ensures consistency of series and definitions. Computes data collected using statistical and econometric techniques and develops summary analysis, including summary tables and charts for various reports. Develops and maintains comprehensive and fully documented cross-country databases in accordance with Fund-wide data management requirements on an ad-hoc basis. Maintains relevant computer software, and writes, updates, modifies, and executes computer programs for statistical and econometric analysis. Initiates analytical work, especially the econometric analysis, underpinning the work of relevant papers and publications produced by the work unit. Participates in divisional/departmental research projects and drafts targeted notes on selected issues of relevance to the division's /department’s work program. Participates in occasional departmental missions and liaises with country authorities, academia, or financial institutions. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Economics, Finance, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science or other related quantitative field, but more competitive candidates would have a Master’s degree in the relevant field. Two years of relevant work experience in a similar role. Proficiency in MS Excel, including basic functions and formula. Proficiency in the use of analytical, statistical and econometric software packages such as STATA, EViews, R, TSP, SPSS, Matlab and SAS. Preferred: Experience working with finance, budget, people analytics, macroeconomic data and writing macroeconomic research reports. Experience and ability to use a range of visual presentation tools such as PowerPoint, MS Excel charts, Tableau, Keynote, Prezi and other similar tools. Familiarity with database management tools such as: Power BI, SQL, MS Access, IBM Cognos BI. Knowledge of Python, C++, and other similar programming tools would be a plus. In addition, the following competencies are critical to the position: Proven ability to manage large and complex databases and develop summary analysis, including summary tables and charts, and sound analytical and problem-solving skills, including a knowledge of statistical applications and techniques. Sound organizational and data management skills, and ability to handle several responsibilities and work under tight time constraints. Ability to work without direct supervision, paying close attention to details and bearing independent responsibility for data accuracy. Proven experience in dealing with all levels of staff in responding to a wide range of inquiries. Ability to use tact, discretion, and sound judgment when dealing with clients and in handling confidential information. item.title: Research Analyst under the Research Analyst Program (RAP)
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Fund is currently seeking talented and motivated individuals with strong quantitative and analytical skills to join its Research Analyst Program (RAP). This program offers a unique opportunity for recent graduates to gain useful entry-level analyst experience and contribute to the IMF's important research and analytical projects before pursuing graduate studies. The RAP is limited to a two-year contractual period. All positions are located at the IMF Headquarters in downtown Washington, D.C. with Research Analysts in the RAP hired on a wide geographical basis. Job Summary As a RAP participant, you will contribute to, and support the operational and policy work of Fund economists. RAP participants may be asked to conduct research, collect and compile information, access and manipulate macroeconomic data from a wide range of sources. The RAP candidate will be expected to maintain and update economic, financial, and statistical databases, conduct quantitative data analysis utilizing econometric and other statistical tools, evaluate economic, financial or statistical relationships in databases, analyze economic time series data, and design systems to facilitate interfaces or to transfer data between external and in-house databases. As a research analyst, you will collaborate with economists and others on various projects and stay up to date with the latest developments in economics and related topics. This opportunity may meet PREDOC requirements for applications to subsequent academic study. Minimum Qualifications: •Recent completion of a bachelor's degree in economics, computer science, statistics, mathematics, finance, data science or other related quantitative field is required. Candidates with advanced degrees in the same relevant field may be considered with limited combined professional experience. •A cumulative GPA of at least 3.5/4.0 (or equivalent for international diplomas) in both the principal field of study and in the overall program. •Ability to work independently under minimum supervision and be accountable for the accuracy of both data and programs. •Proficiency in software applications such as Microsoft Office (specifically Excel and PowerPoint), econometric packages such as STATA, EViews, MATLAB and other statistical and analytical tools. •Knowledge of programming languages like Python and R are desirable. •Working knowledge of Tableau, familiarity with other data visualization tools, especially PowerBI, or Python/R based, or web design are desirable. •Strong analytical and quantitative skills. •Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English. • Proficiency in other languages is a plus. Application Instructions: Applications from all geographical areas are welcome for the RAP. •Upload your unofficial/official transcript verifying your current/final GPA in your undergraduate studies along with your resume and cover letter in your application. Without uploading proof of GPA or an equivalent indication of academic achievement, your application may not be considered. •Note that only those identified for an assignment will be contacted to discuss their interest and availability by the hiring manager. item.title: Resident Advisor (External Sector Statistics, CARTAC-Barbados) - STABP
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The IMF Statistics Department (STA) and the IMF Caribbean Regional Technical Assistance Centre (CARTAC) have an opening for a Resident Advisor on External Sector Statistics (ESS). The selected candidate for this position will develop statistical capacities in CARTAC members to compile and disseminate ESS according to Balance of Payments and International Investment Position Manual, sixth edition ( BPM6 ) and support their preparation to transition to BPM7 . The Resident Advisor will be based in Bridgetown, Barbados , where CARTAC is located, and will work in a team environment in CARTAC and in close coordination with staff in STA’s Balance of Payments Division at the IMF Headquarters (STABP). The Resident Advisor’s initial appointment will be for one year with the possibility of extensions subject to performance, business needs and funding. Ideally, the successful candidate would assume the position in April 2027 to facilitate a short overlap with the incumbent Resident Advisor who is scheduled to conclude her appointment at end-April 2027 . DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES The Resident Advisor will be primarily responsible for providing and overseeing technical assistance (TA) and training in ESS with the objective of strengthening the CARTAC members’ capacity to compile and disseminate accurate and reliable ESS for decision making. Areas of work include: Organizing and delivering TA missions and regional workshops in ESS (both in-person and virtual); Managing and backstopping short-term experts’ TA missions on balance of payments, international investment position (IIP), external debt, international reserves, remittances, and other ESS; Facilitating activities carried out by, and promoting collaboration among, government and regional agencies in the development of such statistics; Coordinating TA activities with STABP, relevant IMF departments (in particular with the Western Hemisphere Department), and, where appropriate, other international and regional agencies providing capacity development (CD) in ESS; Maintaining the IMF’s Results-Based Management (RBM) log frames outlining program objectives and specific outputs for the CARTAC members; Collaborating with other CARTAC resident advisors (in particular with the CARTAC Resident Advisor on Real Sector Statistics) with a view towards building synergies with other IMF CD areas supported by CARTAC. The Resident Advisor will work under the general direction of the CARTAC Director and the technical direction of STABP. QUALIFICATIONS : The successful candidate must have : A post-graduate university degree in a relevant discipline (statistics, economics, finance, business administration, mathematics or other relevant fields); A proven record of strong analytical and technical skills on ESS compilation and methodology; A minimum of 10 years of practical experience in compiling and disseminating balance of payments, IIP, and external debt statistics; Experience negotiating with country authorities; Strong influencing, diplomatic and interpersonal skills, and a drive for results; Strong English oral and written communication skills; A willingness to travel extensively to CARTAC members. The successful candidate should be able to develop and maintain effective relations with national authorities at a senior level and effectively transfer technical knowledge. Experience in organizing and conducting training courses and workshops (including in a virtual or hybrid setting); demonstrated project management skills; familiarity with results-based management, preferably in a capacity development environment; and a knowledge of macro-relevant external sector issues specific to the region are strong assets. Knowledge and experience on emerging topics further elaborated in BPM7 and 2025 SNA , such as globalization, digital economy, and climate-related issues, would be a plus. The CARTAC membership is Anguilla, Antigua & Barbuda, Aruba, The Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands, Curaçao, Dominica, the Eastern Caribbean Currency Union, Grenada, Guyana, Haiti, Jamaica, Montserrat, Sint Maarten, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent & The Grenadines, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago, and Turks and Caicos Islands. item.title: Projects Analyst (Contractual) - IMFFA/IMFRA
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Fund seeks a highly organized and experienced Projects Analyst to administer the work programs of the IMF Family Association (IMFFA) and the IMF Retirees & Alumni Association (IMFRA), as well as support the Fund’s Human Resources Department (HRD). The IMFFA provides a welcoming and supportive community for families of staff members; it offers spouses and families of Fund employees a variety of social programs, services, and events. The IMFRA helps current and future Fund retirees and alumni navigate retirement-related topics, represents their interests, fosters cooperation between the Association and the Fund, and helps retirees and alumni stay in touch with each by organizing social, educational, and other activities. The incumbent formally reports to HRD’s Organizational Change Management Unit and performs support work for both associations on behalf of the IMF. The IMF retains overall responsibility for the employment relationship, including hiring, promotion and termination decisions. Under Fund oversight, on a day-to-day operational basis, the role will support the Boards of Directors of IMFFA and IMFRA. Currently, both associations are working on a hybrid basis, with some days of in-office work at IMF Headquarters and others remotely. The position’s workload typically requires 40 hours a week, allocated equally between the two organizations. Occasionally, events may require additional hours or work on evenings and weekends. During periods of reduced IMFFA and IMFRA activity, the incumbent may also support the work of HRD’s Organizational Change Management Division, which includes employee engagement, health & wellness, support for diversity and inclusion, and internal communications initiatives. Duties and Responsibilities Under Fund oversight, in close contact with the IMFFA and IMFRA Boards, the successful candidate will: Serve as the designated Fund employee liaison for IMFFA and IMFRA activities requiring access to Fund systems, records, communications platforms, or administrative processes, ensuring that such functions are carried out by a Fund employee in accordance with Fund policies and access controls. Serve as the primary point of contact for both associations, and provide excellent customer service, including responding to inquiries and information requests. Build strong relationships with key IMF departments and, as appropriate, forward communications to IMFFA/IMFRA Board members or relevant Fund offices, providing timely follow-up and coordinating responses to requests. Where appropriate, plan, support and deliver work programs and activities. Organize and coordinate meetings and videoconferences. Support tracking and follow-up of Board decisions, actions and timelines. Create and maintain administrative, financial, governance and programmatic files/folders. Support onboarding process for new Board members, including onboarding materials and relevant administrative arrangements. Provide support for meetings, seminars, workshops, excursions and social events. Support Board Chairs when needed. Manage planning and delivery of events with the provision of detailed administrative and logistical support. Receive, process, submit reimbursement claims and follow up until payment is processed. Manage budgets. Timely processing, registration and admission of members and maintenance of membership records. Proactively ensure IMFFA/IMFRA Board members are updated on Fund initiatives of relevance to staff families or retirees and alumni, respectively. Maintain IMFFA and IMFRA websites and social media channels; organize and deliver email and social media communications to members. Where appropriate, plan, support and deliver IMFFA and IMFRA publications, including proofreading, editing, design and dissemination of materials to target audiences. Coordinate procurement related and administrative arrangements with vendors, instructors, speakers and other service providers, including required documentation and follow-up with relevant IMFFA/IMFRA and Fund offices. Support HRD Change Management Division through effective project coordination, stakeholder engagement, visual communications, and administrative support. Preferred Skills and Experience The position requires a highly proactive self-starter able to manage a diverse workload and support day-to-day operations of the two associations effectively. The selected candidate should demonstrate: Experience in supporting project management activities and project delivery Strong interpersonal skills, including tact, patience, and discretion in dealing with a broad range of people from diverse nationalities, age groups and circumstances. Experience in scheduling and organizing in-person and virtual meetings and conferences. Strong IT skills and knowledge of Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, Outlook, Teams), Adobe PDF and virtual meeting software (Zoom, Webex). Familiarity with e-mail applications (such as Mailchimp), social media platforms (LinkedIn, Facebook, Twitter), JotForm, Canva, and willingness to learn new skills and embrace new platforms where required. Administrative experience, including office management. Strong organizational skills and a track record of managing multiple and competing priorities successfully and professionally, and with minimal levels of supervision. Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English. Proficiency in other languages is highly advantageous. Minimum Qualifications A combination of training and experience equivalent to completion of a secondary school education, supplemented by a minimum of four years of relevant experience, is required. This is a one-year contractual appointment. Contractual appointments at the IMF are renewable for up to four years of cumulative contractual service, pending incumbent's performance, budget availability, and continuous business need. item.title: Communications Analyst/Sr. Communications Analyst - (COMPC) – (Contractual)
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. The Communications Department (COM) is the International Monetary Fund’s strategic center for communications. It develops and coordinates external and internal communications strategy, shapes the Fund’s key messages, advises IMF Management and staff on how best to convey key messages, and monitors and responds to what people outside the IMF say about the institution and its activities. The Policy Communications Division (COMPC) works with other COM divisions and the Front Office to develop IMF messages and share them with policymakers, academics, the media, civil society, students, and the wider public. The Division produces the IMF Blog , Finance & Development (F&D) Magazine , Country Focus , the Weekend Read newsletter, the IMF's Factsheet Series , podcasts , videos , and social media campaigns. COMPC uses audience data to assess the impact of these products and strengthen its content and distribution strategies. Job Summary Leads digital marketing campaigns that help IMF content reach and engage key audiences, and manages publishing and production across COMPC’s products. Uses audience analytics, digital optimization, and AI-assisted tools to strengthen the reach and impact of COMPC products. Brings strong editorial instincts to how content is selected, packaged, and presented for digital audiences. The role also includes the administrative work needed to deliver divisional projects and products effectively. We expect applicants to have intellectual curiosity about economics, public policy, and international affairs, and a strong interest in the IMF’s role and mandate. Under the general supervision of the Division’s managers, the specific responsibilities of this contractual position include: Developing and running digital marketing campaigns for COMPC’s products across web, email, newsletters, social media, and other channels. Managing the publishing and production of content for the IMF Blog, Finance & Development, Country Focus, the Weekend Read, Factsheets, podcasts, and videos. This includes staging and publishing content in the IMF’s content-management system, as well as managing editorial calendars, production schedules, reviews, and distribution. Supporting broader COMPC administrative work and assisting other divisional and departmental efforts. Helping package and present editorial content effectively for digital audiences, working with editors and other colleagues on content selection, visuals, sequencing, links, and connections across products. Using audience data and digital optimization to strengthen content and distribution strategies. This includes monitoring performance across digital channels, identifying relevant trends, and applying search engine optimization (SEO), metadata, email-marketing, and generative engine optimization (GEO) to help IMF content reach relevant audiences and appear in search and AI-generated answers. Using AI-assisted tools and automation to improve digital marketing, production processes, audience engagement, and administrative work, while maintaining appropriate editorial judgment and quality control. Coordinating projects and day-to-day operations, working with other divisions and departments as well as external partners. Responsibilities include project-related administrative work such as procurement and vendor coordination, budget processes, event logistics, production tracking, and timely delivery. Requirements Educational development, typically acquired by the completion of a university degree, or equivalent, in Communications, International Relations, Languages, or a related field, supplemented by a minimum of three (3) years of relevant work experience, is required. Alternatively, a minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience at Grade A06, or equivalent, is required. Other Qualifications Demonstrated experience in developing and delivering digital marketing or audience-engagement campaigns, preferably for a policy, research, media, or other knowledge-based organization. Excellent command of written English and strong editorial instincts, with a good eye for content selection, presentation, visuals, and effective digital packaging. Experience with digital publishing and content-management systems; familiarity with Sitecore would be an advantage. Experience with email marketing, social media publishing, web or audience analytics tools such as Adobe Analytics, and visual design tools such as Canva is also desirable. Knowledge of SEO and other digital optimization practices, and experience in using data to assess performance and improve communications strategies. Familiarity with GEO, content metadata, AI-assisted communications, and workflow automation would be an advantage. Excellent project-management and organizational skills, including the ability to manage competing priorities, coordinate stakeholders, and deliver time-sensitive work in a fast-paced international environment. Intellectual curiosity about economics, public policy, and international affairs, and a strong interest in the IMF’s role and mandate. Strong interpersonal skills, good judgment, openness to feedback, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively across teams. Only candidates who are currently residing in the Washington DC metro area will be considered. This is a one-year contractual appointment. Contractual appointments at the IMF are renewable for up to four years of cumulative contractual service, pending incumbent's performance, budget availability, and continuous business need. item.title: 2027 Fund Internship Program (FIP) - Economists
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. Work on real research. In one summer. The Fund Internship Program (FIP) offers PhD students in economics an outstanding opportunity to contribute to the work of one of the world's leading international financial institutions. As a Fund intern, you'll apply your economic research skills to real-world policy questions that matter to the IMF's 191 member countries. You'll work alongside experienced IMF economists, gain hands-on research experience, strengthen your analytical skills, and build a professional network in a uniquely international environment. Many interns present their findings to IMF staff, and some see their work published internally. If you're passionate about macroeconomics, international policy, and research that can make a global impact, the Fund Internship Program could be your next step. About the Program Over 10 to 12 weeks, you'll contribute to an individual research or project assignment while working alongside experienced IMF staff at IMF Headquarters in Washington, D.C. The internship provides practical experience, exposure to the IMF's work, and the opportunity to apply your academic knowledge to real-world policy and operational challenges. To learn more about the Fund Internship Program and hear from previous interns, visit the Fund Internship Program page on IMF Careers. Eligibility To be considered for the 2027 Fund Internship Program - Economists, you must: Be within one to two years of completing a PhD in macroeconomics or a related field. Be enrolled as a student at the time of the internship and return to your academic studies afterward. Be under the age of 32 when the internship begins in June 2027. Demonstrate excellent written and spoken English. Possess strong analytical, quantitative, and computer skills. Application Requirements As part of your online application, you must complete the technical questionnaire and upload the following documents: Curriculum Vitae (CV) or Resume Statement of Interest or Cover Letter explaining your motivation for applying to the IMF Evidence of current student status and academic performance , including either: A recent transcript from your current university program, or A letter from your university confirming active enrollment and recent grades. Incomplete applications will not be considered. Only candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted by a member of the FIP recruitment team. Previous participants in the Fund Internship Program are not eligible and should not reapply. Frequently Asked Questions Is the internship paid? Yes. The Fund Internship Program is a full-time, paid internship requiring 40 hours of work per week. How long is the internship? Internships last between 10 and 12 weeks. When do internships begin? The start of 2027 internship is June 7, 2027 (ending August 27, 2027). What visa support does the IMF provide? If you are not a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or otherwise authorized to work in the United States, you will require a G4 visa. The IMF will provide the documentation needed to support your visa application with U.S. authorities. Does the IMF provide housing? No. Interns are responsible for arranging and securing their own housing accommodation. Resources and guidance may be shared with selected interns during the onboarding process. Will I be notified when my application is received? Yes. You will receive an automated confirmation after submitting your application. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further consideration. Are there exceptions to the age limit? The only exception is for time spent in mandatory military service. item.title: Economist Program 2027
item.description: Work for the IMF. Work for the World. Economist Program (EP) 2027 Work on real policy. From day one. What could your research achieve beyond academia? As an Economist Program participant, you will help countries tackle complex economic challenges. From your first assignment, you will contribute to policy analysis, country work, and research that informs the IMF’s work across its 191 member nations. You will join experienced economists working on real-world policy questions. Depending on your assignment, you may analyze economic developments, assess risks, develop policy options, contribute to country engagement, or conduct research that supports policy decisions. If you are completing or have recently completed a PhD and want to turn rigorous economic research into practical policy advice, the Economist Program could be your next step in a long-term economist career. After successfully completing the three-year program, EPs who demonstrate strong and consistent performance are typically absorbed into the IMF as open-ended economists through vacancies advertised across departments, continuing their careers at the Fund. Program at a Glance Duration: Three years Path after the program: Successful EPs are typically absorbed into IMF departments based on strong and consistent performance during the program. Structure: Two departmental assignments Location: IMF Headquarters in Washington, D.C. Start date: September 2027 Candidate profile: Recent PhD graduates and candidates within one year of completing a PhD Focus: Country work, macroeconomic policy, research, and capacity development The two assignments provide broad exposure to the IMF’s work and help you build a strong foundation in macroeconomic policy and surveillance. To learn more about the program and hear from current and former EP economists, visit the Economist Program page on IMF Careers. What You’ll Work On Your responsibilities will depend on your department and assignment. Your work may include: Country work Analyze economic developments and risks for one or more countries or a region. Contribute to IMF country engagement, including Article IV consultations and IMF-supported programs. Help develop policy advice tailored to a country’s economic circumstances. Policy analysis and advice Assess fiscal, monetary, exchange rate, financial sector, and external sector policies. Examine macro-financial linkages and risks to economic stability. Analyze fiscal and external debt sustainability. Contribute to policy and program design. Support work on economic governance, trade, and regional integration. Research Conduct analytical work and research related to IMF policy priorities. Work with other IMF economists on reports, working papers, and policy publications. Apply economic theory, quantitative methods, and data analysis to real-world policy questions. Capacity development Help member countries strengthen economic institutions, policies, and technical expertise. Contribute to training and technical assistance based on your assignment and area of expertise. From your first assignment, your work will contribute to policy discussions and practical economic outcomes. Why Join the Economist Program? Real responsibility from day one The EP is not a trainee program. You will be hired as an economist and take on substantive responsibilities from the beginning of your first assignment. Broad exposure Through two departmental assignments, you will gain experience across countries, regions, policy areas, and different parts of the IMF. Challenging, policy-relevant work You will work with experienced economists on complex issues affecting member countries and the global economy. A foundation for your career The program will help you build analytical skills, professional network, and experience as a policy economist. It is designed to provide a strong foundation for a long-term career at the IMF. Eligibility To be considered for the 2027 Economist Program, you must: Be a recent PhD graduate or be within one year of completing a PhD in macroeconomics or a related field. Have a solid understanding of macroeconomics and be able to explain complex economic linkages clearly. Be under 34 years old when the program begins in September 2027. Be a citizen of an IMF member country . Demonstrate excellent written and spoken English. Possess strong analytical, quantitative, and computer skills. The IMF welcomes applicants from a range of economics fields. You do not need to specialize exclusively in macroeconomics, but you must have a strong foundation in macroeconomic analysis and an interest in applying economics to policy questions. Recruitment and Selection Process The Economist Program follows an annual recruitment cycle. Applications typically open in late September. Interviews and assessments take place between October and January, offers are typically made in early February, and the incoming cohort begins the following September. Step 1: Preliminary Interview Shortlisted candidates are invited to a 30 to 40-minute preliminary interview. You will provide a high-level overview of your research and discuss economic topics related to the IMF’s work. The interview also considers your analytical thinking, communication, and interpersonal skills. Step 2: Supporting Materials Following the preliminary interview, you may be asked to provide: Your most recent PhD program transcript. Three academic references. A research paper of publishable standard or one or two chapters from your dissertation. Academic references cannot be provided by current IMF staff members. Step 3: Panel Interview and Written Assessment Selected candidates are invited to an in-person panel interview with two or three senior IMF economists and a Human Resources officer. The panel assesses: Knowledge of monetary, fiscal, balance of payments, and financial sector issues. Analytical ability and policy judgment. Written and oral communication. Interpersonal skills. The ability to explain complex economic issues clearly and in a structured way. Candidates also complete a 90-minute written assessment. The assessment evaluates written communication and the ability to develop a clear, well-structured response under time constraints. Step 4: Final Review Candidates who reach the panel stage are referred to an internal committee of senior staff for final review. The committee considers the full set of assessment results. The panel interview and research paper review receive the greatest weight in the final decision. Frequently Asked Questions Do I have to be a macroeconomist to apply? No. The IMF looks for adaptable economists who can learn new fields and bring different perspectives to its work. You must have a solid grounding in macroeconomics and understand the IMF’s work, but EP economists come from a range of fields, including finance, labor economics, development economics, and gender economics. Will I be able to conduct research? Yes. Research and analytical work are important parts of the IMF’s work. IMF economists publish reports and working papers and contribute to books, journals, and other publications. You will have opportunities to exchange ideas and collaborate with economists working across many fields. The time available for independent research will depend on your assignment, the relevance of the research to the IMF’s work, and your ability to balance research with other responsibilities. Is the Economist Program a trainee program? No. EP participants are hired as economists and take on substantive responsibilities from the beginning of their assignments. How long is the program? The program lasts three years and includes two departmental assignments. What happens after the three-year Economist Program? After successfully completing the three-year program, EPs who demonstrate strong and consistent performance are typically absorbed into IMF departments as economists through job vacancies advertised by economist departments. The program is designed to provide broad exposure, build policy experience, and support a long-term economist career at the IMF. What materials may be requested after the preliminary interview? You may be asked to provide: A transcript from your PhD program. Three academic references. A research paper or one or two dissertation chapters. Are there exceptions to the age limit? The only exception is for time spent completing mandatory military service. What visa support does the IMF provide? If you are not a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or otherwise authorized to work in the United States, you will require a G-4 visa. The IMF will provide the documentation needed to support your visa application with the U.S. authorities. Ready to Launch Your Career as an IMF Economist? Apply your research to real policy questions. Build experience across countries, departments, and economic issues. Join a global community of economists working to help countries address complex challenges. Apply for the 2027 Economist Program.
